Finally clued in to the fact that this isn’t just another shot of yet another fantastic Lake Huron sunset.
It’s actually artificially filtered by a massive plume of wildfire smoke coming from far away. Thanks, Alberta and Saskatchewan, for helping create the climate change that fuels those fires.
🙄
Smoke from Canadian wildfires made for some interesting shots of Lake Superior. #camping #minnesota #photography

Hi folks. I've been away, enjoying some beach time on the shores of mighty Lake Huron. Here's a wildfire smoke influenced sundown shot from last night. I look forward to catching up with your recent posts. Cheers! #photography #blueskyphotography #sunset #sunsets #lakehuron #canada #wildfiresmoke

Simply titled 'smoke' because for most of the summer here in Ontario our sunsets were hazy. Lake Huron on the peninsula still rules in terms of watching them. Also, I vowed never to paint a sunset and look what this landscape made me do.

The low sun angle really emphasizes the density of smoke over the western Great Lakes region. Wouldn't be surprised if we can safely* stare directly at the sun as a dim orange disc before sunset. *This statement has not been skeeted by a trained professional

It sure looks beautiful, but living here on Sturgeon Bay, surrounded by Lake Michigan in Northeast Wisconsin, we all realize what’s causing the sun to look beautifully orange like that, it’s the same smoke and pollutants that they’re telling us to stay inside because of the Canadian wildfires. 🤷🏻‍♀️
Photo: Smoke from Canadian wildfires on the west edge of Lake Michigan changing dawn light. We must hang together or the rich will surely continue to hang us separately.
